excerpt: In a vacuum, heat is transferred only by radiation and conduction with no convection. A deployable radiator is stowed during transit or when the radiator is not needed and deployed when excess heat dissipation is required.
note: Backs orbital thermal rejection (radiate-only constraint), deployable radiator panels, heat-pipe transport, and coating degradation ('Coatings will darken due to atomic oxygen bombardment ... This will increase the solar absorptance values'). No verbatim TVAC-test sentence on page; that sub-claim is the weakest fit but core thermal claims hold.

excerpt: Single Event Latchup (SEL) - a condition which causes loss of device functionality due to a single event induced high current state. An SEL may or may not cause permanent device damage, but requires power strobing of the device to resume normal device operation.
note: PDF slide deck (NASA NEPP 'Radiation Effects 101'). Backs SEE/SEU/SEL/latchup watchdog-recovery, TID shielding ('Total Ionizing Dose (TID) ... Can partially mitigate with shielding'), ECC/data-integrity ('error detection and correction (EDAC) on large memory arrays'), parts selection (RHA), and ground radiation test campaign ('All devices with unknown characteristics should be ground radiation tested (TID and SEE)').
